caption: Fig. 5.1: Shapes of different coordination polyhedra. M represents the central atom/ion and L, a unidentate ligand.
note: text_layer null; read from the image. The caption is printed INSIDE target_box_in_crop over three physical lines ('Fig. 5.1: Shapes of different coordination polyhedra. M' / 'represents the central atom/ion and L, a unidentate' / 'ligand.') and is joined here with single spaces; its last line is grazed by the bottom edge of the box but is fully legible. Ordering: the figure is five independent structural drawings side by side, so the labels are listed structure by structure from left to right (not interleaved row-wise across the five), each structure's own labels in spatial order top-left to bottom-right, immediately followed by that structure's printed name. The drawings carry only the single letters 'M' (central atom) and 'L' (ligand), repeated: octahedral has six L around one M, tetrahedral four L, square planar four L, trigonal bipyramidal five L, square pyramidal five L -- 24 'L' labels and five 'M' labels in all, each one genuinely printed on the page. Known structural loss: a flat list cannot show which L and M belong to which drawing, nor the stereochemistry the drawing conveys (plain lines in the plane, bold wedges toward the reader, hatched wedges away from it), which is the entire point of the figure; the per-structure grouping above is the closest the schema allows. Over-included by the crop and excluded as belonging to other blocks: the paragraph above ('attached to the central atom/ion defines a coordination polyhedron about the central atom. The most common coordination polyhedra are octahedral, square planar and tetrahedral. For example, [Co(NH3)6]3+ is octahedral, [Ni(CO)4] is tetrahedral and [PtCl4]2- is square planar. Fig. 5.1 shows the shapes of different coordination polyhedra.'), the heading '(g) Oxidation number of central atom' and the paragraph under it ('The oxidation number of the central atom in a complex is defined as the charge it would carry if all the ligands are removed along with the electron pairs that are shared with the central atom. The oxidation number is represented by a Roman numeral in parenthesis...'). A faint diagonal 'NCERT / not to be republished' watermark crosses the figure without obscuring it.
